To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the social capital approach can be used to evaluate investments that have a basic needs externality; (2) the social capital externality is an externality that is positive and should be included in the evaluation of the project; (3) this externality is not included in the financial evaluation; (4) the value of the social capital externalty is greater than the financial evaluation; and (5) the social capital evaluation can be used to justify the project.
the social evaluation of the investment project should include a measure of the basic needs externalities that are created by the project.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical framework for evaluating the social capital externality created when investments are made that improve the welfare of the poor in a community.
developing a theoretical framework for measuring the value of the basic needs externalities of investments, and applying this framework to a case study.

the social evaluation of investments that create a social benefit that is external to the project itself, but which is created by the investment and which is a result of the social capital that exists in the community.

social capital is important for the evaluation of investments.

the basic needs externalty is an important component of the economic evaluation of investments, that it is not easy to quantify, but that the methodology presented in this paper can be used to obtain a rough estimate of this externality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the basic needs approach is a powerful tool for social evaluation of investments.
the social evaluation of investment projects should take into consideration the basic needs externals created by the project.
we have developed a new theoretical framework that is capable of evaluating the social welfare impact of investments in a developing country.

social capital can be a very important factor in the social evaluation of investments.
